outcome: No progress on the Halperin conjecture (Serre spectral sequence collapse for fibrations with rationally elliptic, nonzero-Euler-characteristic fiber) has been found dated after 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open in general, with the most recent substantive progress (Kennard–Wu, formal dimensions up to 20) predating the frozen revision.
summary: The frozen Wikipedia bullet describes the Halperin conjecture on collapse of the rational Serre spectral sequence for fibrations whose fiber is rationally elliptic with non-zero Euler characteristic (equivalently, via Meier's algebraic reformulation: a positively elliptic algebra admits no non-trivial derivation of negative degree). The last substantive progress on this conjecture is Kennard and Wu's extension of the formal-dimension verification from 16 to 20 (arXiv:2104.04086, posted April 2021, published in Communications in Algebra 51(8), 2023) — this predates the 26 January 2024 freeze and is already reflected in pre-2024 literature, matching the triage's finding. I re-ran the triage's queries plus several additional ones targeting later formal-dimension extensions ('22', '24'), AI/algorithmic angles, and general 'proof/solved' phrasing, and checked the live Wikipedia article, which itself still states the conjecture was open '[a]s of 2019' with no newer update recorded. Two 2025 arXiv papers surfaced in searches (2503.01123, a March 2025 paper on sequential parametrized topological complexity, and 2507.02590, a July 2025 paper giving algorithms to compute LS category and the Ginsburg invariant for elliptic spaces) both sit in the same rational-homotopy-of-elliptic-spaces neighborhood but neither addresses the Halperin conjecture itself — the first doesn't mention it at all, and the second's algorithmic contribution is about different invariants (LS category, Ginsburg invariant), not the derivation/collapse question the conjecture poses, and it does not use AI/ML methods (classical algorithms only). No AI involvement of any kind was found near this problem. I conclude nothing has happened to this problem in the window, and no AI system has come near it.
competing_reading: None found. The 2507.02590 paper works in an adjacent algorithmic corner of elliptic-space theory and could in principle be read as tangential progress on the surrounding toolkit, but it does not touch the derivation/spectral-sequence-collapse statement that constitutes the conjecture, so it is a related-but-distinct question rather than a case or variant of this one.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that either (a) proves the general collapse/no-negative-derivation statement, (b) extends the formal-dimension verification beyond 20, or (c) settles a genuinely new special case (e.g., a new class of homogeneous or Kähler-like spaces) not already covered by Meier, Shiga-Tezuka, or Lupton's pre-2024 results.
